stemMd: Which pair represents isotopes of the same element?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Atoms with 8 and 10 protons but 8 neutrons each

options.label: B
options.textMd: Atoms with 8 protons and either 8 or 10 neutrons

options.label: C
options.textMd: Molecules with the same mass but different formulas

options.label: D
options.textMd: An atom with 8 protons and one with 8 electrons only

options.label: E
options.textMd: Atoms with identical protons and neutrons but different electron numbers

explanationMd: Isotopes share an atomic number and therefore the same proton count, but differ in neutron count. The two oxygen atoms satisfy both conditions. A change in electrons produces an ion; a change in protons changes the element.

distractorRationale.a: Different proton numbers identify different elements.
distractorRationale.d: Electron count alone does not establish the same element or different neutron counts.
distractorRationale.c: Isotopes are atomic forms of an element, not arbitrary equal-mass molecules.
distractorRationale.e: That describes different ionization states, not different isotopes.
